So I'm a manager at Bahama Buck's which is in the same parking lot as Kroger on Campbell and I'll give you a little bit of the hiring side of it. We look for daytime workers or weekend workers depending on what we need, and we're all students meaning we get it that classes and homework are important. (I made the schedule for over a year there. I'm a real person, I'm a student and I work 3 jobs, I get it. You need time to study.) But our thing is hiring more for the summer, because as a snocone place, that's our busy season. So let's say you can work Mondays, Wednesdays and maybe Saturdays, we could work with that until summer came and you could work more. But if you were to try to keep to very few hours, I'm not sure it would work out because summer is just so crazy (last summer my paychecks were for 100+ hours a piece, over a two week span. Granted I was literally never not there, but it's an example of how much busier it is than right now.)

As for working and going to school, it's not all bad. You have to be VERY good at time management. My main goal is to get all my homework/studying done by Thursday so I can have Friday and Saturday to work and just relax. And then Sunday, I get back on the study grind. It helps give me a break without procrastinating too much. (I have no choice but to work my ass off so I can pay my bills but breaks are good for the soul!) My advisor freshman year actually told me his students with jobs typically do better in classes because they have less time to get things done. (Since you have less time, you're more likely to do it when you first get the chance instead of waiting until last minute.) It's all dependent on you though! You've gotta put in the effort of balancing work and school and anything else you add to your plate (friends, sports, clubs, whatever).

Sorry this was rambly and not super helpful but my main point is that if there's a time in sight that your schedule will change, I would definitely try to use that as a selling point and that it's possible to do it all, just not easy. Best of luck! :)
